Modern.brandNameRationale: Gerardus Mercator's 1569 cylindrical projection is the most-used map projection in history. Mercator died in 1594 — the eponym is fully public-domain. 'Lab' signals the experimental, contemporary-geospatial posture.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern cartography has split between mass GIS platforms and a small editorial-cartography cohort. The opening is for a studio that anchors on the foundational projection work and applies it to contemporary publishing and planning briefs.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Stamen Design (stamen.com) holds the editorial-cartography slot. Carto (carto.com) is the GIS-platform peer. Mapbox (mapbox.com) sets the developer-mapping bar. We sit closer to Stamen in editorial discipline.
Modern.positioningStatement: Modern cartography lab — web maps, projections, custom geospatial work for publishers and planners.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Editors, urban planners, publishing-house art directors. Commission one map every six months.
behaviors: Specifies datum and projection in the brief

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Mercator Lab in a precise modern grotesk with a small graticule (latitude-longitude grid) mark above. The graticule alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for coordinates and scale bars
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the coordinates, scale, and projection metadata.

Luxury.tagline: Hand-coloured atlases, in the Atlas Maior tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Willem Blaeu and Joan Blaeu were Amsterdam's pre-eminent 17th-century mapmakers. Their Atlas Maior (1662–65) is the most luxurious atlas ever produced. The Blaeu name is public-domain (the cartographers died centuries ago); 'House' closes the brand as a contemporary atelier.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury cartography is rare and serves the private library, the yacht owner, the institutional collector. The opening is for a small Amsterdam-style house producing hand-coloured, leather-bound atlases in the Atlas Maior tradition.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: London Map Fair dealers (e.g. Daniel Crouch Rare Books, crouchrarebooks.com) hold the rare-map peer slot. Altea Antique Maps (alteamaps.com) sits in the antique-maps peer position. Old World Auctions (oldworldauctions.com) plays the historical-cartography peer. We sit between these as a contemporary maker in the Atlas Maior tradition.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Luxury Amsterdam-tradition hand-coloured atlases for private libraries and collectors.

targetAudience.primary: 55 to 80. Multi-generational collector. Owns a private library. Commissions one atlas every two years.

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Blaeu House set in a classical Dutch roman with a small cartouche mark drawn from the Atlas Maior tradition. The mark sits on the leather cover and the certificate.

typography.primary: Adobe Garamond for the wordmark and atlases
typography.secondary: Adobe Caslon for body and correspondence
typography.rationale: Two related serifs in the 17th-century Dutch printing tradition. The brand reads like a contemporary atlas in the Atlas Maior lineage.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: The Prime Meridian (Greenwich, established 1851; international agreement 1884) is the foundational line of longitude. The word is the line; the brand is the geometry.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal cartography has been crowded with line-only Etsy prints. The opening underneath is a studio that strips cartography to its abstract grammar — meridian and parallel, nothing else.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Stamen Design (stamen.com) holds the editorial-modern slot translated to minimal. Atelier Brückner (atelier-brueckner.com) plays the considered-design peer. Areaware Maps (areaware.com) is the small-format peer. We sit further out — lines only, single colour.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Minimal cartography. Lines only. Single colour. The geometry of the grid.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Designers, architects, publishers. Buy one piece every two years. Care about the line weight.

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark — Meridian set in a humanist sans with a single vertical line (the meridian) beside it. The line alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and body
typography.rationale: One family. Mono for the latitude-longitude.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: The cadastre is the land-registry map, codified by Napoleon's 1807 cadastral law — the most economically important map type in the world. The phrase is public-domain technical vocabulary; '& Co.' closes the brand as a B2B firm.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate cartography for land records is a serious B2B category — parcels, easements, title-grade base maps. Municipalities, title-insurance underwriters, and utility companies need cadastral-grade accuracy.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Esri (esri.com) is the global GIS giant. Trimble (trimble.com) holds the survey-equipment peer slot. Bentley Systems (bentley.com) plays the infrastructure-mapping peer position. We sit smaller and more cadastral-specific.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Corporate cadastral cartography for municipalities and title underwriters.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 60. Municipal GIS directors, title-insurance underwriters, utility-mapping VPs.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small parcel-grid mark — CADASTRE & CO. set in a tight grotesk above a small grid icon. Reads cleanly on municipal RFPs, GIS-platform documentation, and trade-show banners.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed cadastral documents and contracts
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed municipal documentation.

Creative.brandNameRationale: 'Hic sunt dracones' — the legendary annotation on the 1510 Hunt-Lenox Globe for unknown territory — is the most famous cartographic phrase. The English translation is public-domain historical vocabulary and signals the speculative, fiction-publisher posture.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative cartography has been crowded with literal city-print shops. The opening is for a studio leaning into the unknown-territory aesthetic — speculative maps, fantasy cartography, fiction-publisher commissions.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Stuart Daly Studio (stuart-daly.com) holds the fantasy-cartography peer slot. Daniel Reeve (danielreeve.co.nz) is the film-cartography reference (Lord of the Rings). Atlas Obscura (atlasobscura.com) plays the speculative-geography peer. We sit closer to Reeve in commission posture.
Creative.positioningStatement: Creative cartography for fiction publishers, game studios, and speculative briefs.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Fiction editors, game-studio art directors, role-playing publishers. Commission one map every quarter.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — HERE BE DRAGONS set in a display serif with a small hand-drawn sea-monster mark above. The monster alone is a sticker.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and editorial
typography.secondary: PP Mori for body and product cards
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the manuscript register. Mori keeps the product copy warm.
